themes_detail.label: Rodent infestation spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints in CD 411 spiked to 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 540% increase (z-score: 4.85)—suggesting a potential citywide or district-specific infestation event requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: 4 rodent complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (8-week average)
540% spike in rodent complaints with z-score of 4.85 (statistically significant)
Community Board has requested sanitation infrastructure upgrades year after year, suggesting chronic conditions
reporting_angles: Interview affected residents in Bayside/Douglaston/Little Neck about where rodents are appearing (homes, businesses, parks) and whether complaints to 311 are being addressed
Contact NYC Department of Sanitation about whether this spike is isolated to CD 411 or part of a broader winter infestation trend

themes_detail.label: Mold outbreak in buildings
themes_detail.summary: Mold complaints exploded to 6 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 4700% spike (z-score: 17.76, highest severity)—indicating widespread housing conditions or water infiltration issues tied to seasonal weather or infrastructure failure.
evidence: 6 mold complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (8-week average)—4700% increase
Highest z-score (17.76) of all spikes, indicating extreme statistical anomaly
Converges with water system complaints (421 total over 90 days) and building code enforcement gap noted in repeated CB budget requests for illegal conversion enforcement
reporting_angles: Investigate whether mold spike is tied to recent flooding, burst pipes, or poor drainage in specific neighborhoods (e.g., near Bayside or Douglaston waterfront areas)
Interview tenants about whether landlords are addressing mold reports; check DOB violation records for related building code violations
Examine whether Department of Environmental Protection infrastructure requests in CB budget submissions reflect known water/drainage problems

themes_detail.label: Special Projects Inspection surge
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints surged to 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)—a 380% spike (z-score: 4.91)—possibly indicating unannounced enforcement actions or neighborhood-wide code violations being flagged.
evidence: 3 SPIT complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline
Aligns with 5 active ULURP applications and 535 DOB building permits (mostly alterations) filed in 90 days, suggesting increased scrutiny of construction/code compliance
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Buildings to learn what triggered this week's SPIT activity—is it targeted enforcement in a specific area or routine sweep?
Cross-reference SPIT complaints with active construction permits and ULURP projects to determine if enforcement is tied to development activity

themes_detail.label: Dumpster and waste disposal crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dumpster complaints jumped to 4 LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike), and residential disposal complaints hit 7 LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 average (367% spike)—jointly suggesting severe waste collection or illegal dumping issues affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: 4 dumpster complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (967% increase, z-score: 7.49)
7 residential disposal complaints last week vs. 1.5 weekly baseline (367% increase, z-score: 4.92)
Community Board has requested sanitation infrastructure upgrades annually, indicating chronic service gaps
reporting_angles: Canvass neighborhoods to identify where dumpsters are overflowing or inaccessible; interview residents about missed pickups or illegal dumping
Contact NYC Department of Sanitation to determine if staffing, vehicle breakdown, or route changes caused service disruptions last week
Map complaint locations to identify concentration patterns and check whether specific commercial or residential areas are underserved

themes_detail.label: Street noise and quality decline
themes_detail.summary: Street/sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 10 LAST WEEK vs. 3.2 weekly average (208% spike, z-score: 4.56), while street condition complaints remain the second-highest complaint category at 1393 over 90 days—indicating potential construction, traffic, or infrastructure degradation.
evidence: 10 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 3.2 weekly baseline (208% increase)
Street condition remains #2 complaint category with 1,393 complaints over 90 days
535 DOB building permits filed in 90 days (mostly alterations) may be driving construction noise
reporting_angles: Identify which construction or development projects (from 535 active permits) are generating noise complaints; check if work is occurring outside permitted hours
Interview residents and business owners about whether noise correlates with specific streets (e.g., near Northern Boulevard or 24th Avenue rezoning areas)
